step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows client applications (EC2 instance and Lambda function) connecting to a database proxy solution provided by Heimdall Data. Client database calls route through a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to an Auto Scaling group of Heimdall Proxy EC2 instances. The proxy instances maintain an L1 cache internally and connect to Amazon ElastiCache for a shared/synchronized cache layer. On cache misses, requests are forwarded to Amazon RDS. Management and cache configuration policies are managed via a central Management EC2 server on a separate control plane.

graph.name: Heimdall Data Proxy Architecture on AWS
graph.notes: Heimdall proxy transparently caches database queries across an Auto Scaling group using ElastiCache as L2 cache and connects to RDS for cache misses. Central management server handles control plane config.
